text: Academic Mobility Guidebook A comprehensive guide about exchange opportunities at Nazarbayev University 2026 [Updated] Dear student, This book contains all the information you need to know to get acquainted with exchange opportunities at NU. Please refer to the table of contents below for guidance. At the moment of publishing this material (October 31, 2025), all the processes in regard to mobility programs were factual and based on the then- current partner universities. Please specify your expectations from participating in this program, your motivation and future plans 6 Important Points Before and After Completion When nominated for the exchange, ensure that the courses you plan to take at the Host Institution are discussed with your School’s Academic Manager, approved by the Department Chair or Program Director, and have NU equivalents in order to be officially transferred later. After completing an Academic Exchange or Study Abroad program, the Host Institution must send a physical copy of the official transcript to the Department of Internationalization (DI), which will forward it to the School for credit transfer. Course grades from these programs are not included in the NU CGPA, except in cases of “Fail” or its equivalent. In other words, the system of credit transfer works by the Pass/Fail. The Registrar’s Office does not inform the School of student grades, as the School is already aware. Upon their return, NU outgoing exchange students must start attending classes at NU

grades, as the School is already aware. Upon their return, NU outgoing exchange students must start attending classes at NU within the first week of the new semester. Students are responsible for coordinating with their professors to catch up on any missed coursework. NU does not guarantee that absences due to mobility will be excused. 7 DI or CAC? Students often tend to confuse these two structures because, at first glance, they seem the same as they are closely working with students and providing them with various opportunities. Here is an overview: The Department of Internationalization (DI) promotes and coordinates

with students and providing them with various opportunities. Here is an overview: The Department of Internationalization (DI) promotes and coordinates student mobility programs, and is mainly responsible for the following: Calling for applications Sending documents of selected students to the Host Institutions Approval of exchange programs proposed from outside by students Career Advising Center (CAC) assists NU students with internships, job search, interview skills, resume review, alumni issues, and graduate application, hence: Educating in experiential learning programs Connecting students and alumni with internships provided by the employers Facilitate Internship programs in cooperation with NU schools 8 List of Partner Universities

A: Although programs may provide financial aid and cover the expenses, normally students are expected to pay for: 2-way flight tickets Accommodation Visa Medical Insurance Food Miscellaneous Q: Does NU have Erasmus+ agreements? A: Yes, NU has numerous agreements for Student Mobility programs within the framework of the Erasmus program. Q: Can students find and participate in mobility programs on their own? A: Yes, NU students can participate in Student Mobility programs on their own. However, the respective NU School still has to

Yes, NU students can participate in Student Mobility programs on their own. However, the respective NU School still has to approve the program as credit-bearing. Q: Who announces mobility opportunities? A: Each School announces exchange opportunities via email with all the requirements and set deadlines. Q: How long do student mobility programs usually last? A: The most common period of academic exchange for most students is one semester. However, the duration of student mobility programs can vary, ranging from a few weeks to a full academic year. 12 Q: Are mobility programs free for NU students? A: Mobility opportunities provided

few weeks to a full academic year. 12 Q: Are mobility programs free for NU students? A: Mobility opportunities provided by NU based on NU cooperation links usually include Tuition fee waiver. Other expenses (2-way air fare, accommodation, food expenses/costs, visa fee, medical insurance, miscellaneous expenses and additional university fees) are covered by the student. Q: What are possible challenges along the student mobility program? A: Challenges can include cultural adjustment, language barriers, homesickness, differences in educational systems, administrative complexities related to visa and travel regulations, and financial differences for living expenses. A: There are no restrictions for students with families or dependents. However, visa issues and all the costs for their expenses should be borne by students. Q: Do I need to know the local language to participate in an academic mobility program? A: Many courses at Host Institutions are usually offered in English, while some of them might require proficiency in the local language.
